question: When a residual pure self-attention layer with shared weights is iterated to large depth, what geometric clusters do token representations approach, and how are those limits determined by the value matrix spectrum and input context?

key_findings.claim: In one dimension with positive query-key coupling and value scalar, the self-attention matrix converges to a structured low-rank nearly Boolean limit that concentrates attention on at most three leader tokens.
key_findings.evidence: For distinct initial tokens, Theorem 2.1 proves convergence to the paper's matrix class P; all rows except possibly one become one-hot, with off-pattern coefficients converging doubly exponentially. For almost every initialization the exceptional row is also one-hot, making the limit rank one or two.

anchors.section: Asymptotic low-rankness of the self-attention matrix

key_findings.claim: After the analytically motivated rescaling z_i(t)=exp(-tV)x_i(t), identity-value attention drives every token toward zero or the boundary of an input-dependent convex polytope; generic vertex convergence is observed but not fully proved.
key_findings.evidence: For V equal to the identity and positive-definite Q-transpose-K, Theorem 3.1 constructs a limiting bounded polytope from the shrinking convex hull and proves convergence to its boundary or zero. The locations therefore depend on the starting tokens and attention metric. A separate theorem shows V=-I with QK=I collapses all tokens to the origin.

anchors.section: Clustering toward vertices of convex polytopes

key_findings.claim: For a value matrix with one positive dominant eigenvalue, the dominant eigendirection confines rescaled tokens asymptotically to at most three parallel hyperplanes; with a repeated positive leading eigenspace, the limit becomes a polytope-boundary factor times the complementary subspace.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.2 handles a simple leading eigenvalue separated in modulus under a positive query-key form along its eigenvector and proves convergence of the dominant coordinate to at most three levels. Theorem 5.2 treats a paranormal value matrix with a positive scalar action on the leading invariant subspace and smaller spectral radius off it, yielding distance convergence to (boundary(K) union zero) times the complement.

key_findings.claim: The particle dynamics and their mean-field continuity equation are globally well posed, but the strongest clustering conclusions remain specific to the paper's idealized weight and spectral regimes.
key_findings.evidence: The paper proves existence, uniqueness, compact-support propagation, and Wasserstein stability for the attention continuity equation, then obtains the finite-token ODE as an empirical-measure corollary. Numerical tests with random matrices, two ALBERT heads, non-PSD query-key products, and appended feed-forward maps suggest broader behavior, which the authors explicitly leave as conjectures and open problems.

method.core_idea: Treat tokens as an interacting particle system evolving through residual self-attention depth, remove the dominant linear value growth by a time-dependent change of variables, and characterize the resulting asymptotic geometry with dynamical-systems, convexity, spectral, and mean-field tools.
method.mechanism: Softmax attention defines a non-symmetric all-to-all velocity field. In rescaled coordinates, exponentially amplified dominant eigendirections make attention increasingly selective. Monotonic order in one dimension yields leader matrices; shrinking convex hulls and persistence of outward motion yield polytope boundaries; spectral separation confines dominant coordinates to a few levels while lower eigenspaces contribute residual hyperplane directions.
assumptions: The analysis uses pure single-head residual self-attention with matrices Q, K, and V fixed across depth, as in a weight-sharing idealization.
Most clustering theorems study rescaled tokens exp(-tV)x(t), a mathematical surrogate rather than the actual layer-normalization operator.
The one-dimensional result assumes pairwise-distinct tokens, V>0, and QK>0.
Polytope theorems require positive-definite Q-transpose-K and identity or a structured paranormal value matrix.
The simple-eigenvalue theorem requires a positive leading eigenvalue separated in modulus and positive query-key coupling along its eigenvector.

techniques.role: Represents residual depth as a continuous-time, all-to-all interacting token system.
Factors out exponential growth or decay induced by the value matrix and preserves the attention coefficients.
Constructs the limiting polytope and constrains token accumulation points.
Uses dominant value eigenspaces to identify limiting parallel hyperplanes or polytope-by-subspace sets.
Proves global well-posedness and Wasserstein stability for finite or continuum token distributions.
Tests conjectured extensions and visualizes asymptotic cluster geometry.

evaluations.setting: One-dimensional and small-dimensional synthetic token systems
evaluations.metric: Rank and entry pattern of the attention matrix and number of leader clusters
evaluations.result: Simulations match convergence toward rank-one or rank-two Boolean-like attention and show the same leader pattern in tested higher dimensions, where the theorem is not established.

evaluations.setting: Identity and structured-value dynamics in two, three, and ALBERT-scale dimensions
evaluations.metric: Distance of rescaled tokens to polytope vertices or dominant-eigenvector hyperplanes
evaluations.result: Toy systems rapidly form the predicted polytopes and usually two of the theorem's at most three hyperplanes; negative complementary eigenvalues can make other coordinates oscillate or diverge along those hyperplanes.
evaluations.baseline: Predicted limiting sets from Theorems 3.1, 4.2, and 5.2

evaluations.metric: Whether learned head spectra satisfy the simple-leading-eigenvalue assumptions
evaluations.result: The paper identifies heads 5 and 14 whose value spectra and query-key coupling along the dominant eigenvector satisfy the assumptions of Theorem 4.2.
evaluations.baseline: Random matrices used in the synthetic experiments

evaluations.setting: Numerical extensions beyond positive-definite query-key products and with a two-layer feed-forward map
evaluations.result: Cluster patterns continue in the shown examples, motivating conjectures, but no statistical sweep or theorem establishes robustness.
evaluations.baseline: Pure attention under the proved positive-definite regimes

limitations: Weights are tied across an arbitrarily deep stack; ordinary Transformers learn different matrices at each layer and have finite depth.
The model omits multi-head interactions, feed-forward blocks, biases, positional operations, and actual layer normalization from its theorems.
Most claims concern rescaled coordinates and infinite-time behavior, which need not predict representations at practical depth.
Several results require positive-definite query-key geometry or restrictive value spectra, and higher-dimensional generalizations are sometimes supported only by examples.
The numerical section illustrates mechanisms but is not a task-level evaluation connecting clusters to language performance or semantic leaders.
failure_modes: A complex leading eigenvalue can produce rotation rather than convergence to stationary clusters.
Negative dominant value growth can make rescaled tokens diverge, while V=-I in the canonical case collapses every token to zero.
In higher dimension, pathological configurations invalidate a direct extension of the one-dimensional Boolean low-rank proof.
Even when dominant coordinates cluster, complementary coordinates may diverge along the limiting hyperplanes, so full vectors need not converge.
Multi-head sums or feed-forward nonlinearities can create competing vector fields for which the single-head convex-hull arguments no longer apply.
reusable_insights: Separate trivial value-driven norm growth from relational attention dynamics before interpreting depth trajectories.
Analyze the spectrum and invariant subspaces of learned value matrices alongside attention maps; they predict qualitatively different geometries.
Distinguish low-rank attention weights from converged token representations and from low-rank model parameters.
Use context-dependent limiting sets rather than global fixed prototypes when formalizing token leaders.
Test asymptotic toy-model claims at the actual finite depth, with layer normalization and untied weights, before treating them as mechanisms of trained Transformers.
open_questions: Which clustering or metastability results survive multiple heads with distinct value spectra?
Can actual layer normalization, residual scaling, and feed-forward blocks be incorporated without replacing them by exponential rescaling?
What non-asymptotic depth bounds predict when a finite network first forms and later merges token clusters?
How stable are limiting leaders under untied but slowly varying weights learned across depth?
Do the mathematical clusters correspond reproducibly to syntax, semantics, or task performance in trained language models?
Under what generic higher-dimensional conditions does the attention matrix become Boolean and low rank?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding and Improving Transformer From a Multi-Particle Dynamic System Point of View
competitive_landscape.difference: Lu et al. interpret attention plus feed-forward layers as a numerical splitting method for a convection-diffusion system and design Macaron Net; the reviewed paper focuses on rigorous long-time cluster geometry for a fixed-weight pure-attention flow.

competitive_landscape.title: Attention is Not All You Need: Pure Attention Loses Rank Doubly Exponentially with Depth
competitive_landscape.difference: Dong, Cordonnier, and Loukas prove token uniformity for pure attention without skip connections and show that residual or MLP paths prevent it; this paper includes a residual flow and therefore obtains richer leader, polytope, and hyperplane clusters rather than inevitable rank-one tokens.

competitive_landscape.title: Sinkformers: Transformers with Doubly Stochastic Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Sinkformers replace row-softmax with Sinkhorn normalization to obtain a Wasserstein gradient-flow and heat-diffusion interpretation plus task experiments; the reviewed work retains ordinary row-stochastic softmax and studies its context-dependent asymptotic clusters.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamic metastability in the self-attention model
competitive_landscape.relationship: later direct refinement of the asymptotic cluster picture
competitive_landscape.difference: The later work proves that normalized self-attention can remain near multiple clusters for exponentially long times before ultimately merging to one, showing why finite-depth observations can differ sharply from the infinite-time limit emphasized here.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: this paper is a substantial first rigorous taxonomy of context-dependent cluster geometry for residual softmax attention with tied weights, going beyond both the no-residual rank-collapse theorem and earlier particle analogies. Its convex-polytope and spectral-hyperplane results are mathematically distinctive, and the later metastability result confirms the model's fertility. The connection to practical Transformers remains hypothesis-generating because theorems omit multi-head, untied finite-depth, normalized, feed-forward dynamics and do not validate task semantics.
reviewer_notes: All 55 extracted pages were reviewed, including every theorem statement, the one-dimensional, convex-hull, spectral, and mean-field proofs, numerical methods, ALBERT spectrum example, conjectures, and outlook. Primary competitors and the 2024 metastability follow-up were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23. The review consistently distinguishes proved boundary convergence from empirically observed vertex convergence, and the rescaled token variables from actual layer normalization.
